title: Pacific islands battle dengue fever outbreak, Samoan boy dies in Auckland hospital
summary: A 12-year-old Samoan boy, Misiafa Lene, died of dengue after being medically evacuated to Starship Children’s Hospital in Auckland. Pacific islands including Samoa, Fiji and Tonga are experiencing dengue outbreaks, posing risks to residents and tourists and prompting increased public health warnings.
content:
Misiafa Lene, a 12-year-old boy from Samoa, succumbed to dengue fever in Auckland. He contracted the disease in Samoa and was medically evacuated to Starship Children’s Hospital in Auckland, New Zealand.

The ongoing dengue outbreak across Pacific islands poses risks to residents as well as tourists. Samoa, Fiji and Tonga are among the islands currently dealing with rising case counts and localized outbreaks.

Health officials in the affected islands have reported increased numbers of dengue infections and are urging the public to remain vigilant. Mosquito-control measures, early recognition of symptoms and prompt medical care are being emphasized to reduce severe outcomes.

Medical evacuations to regional centers such as Starship Children’s Hospital highlight constraints in pediatric critical care capacity on some smaller islands. Authorities continue to monitor the situation and advise travelers to take precautions against mosquito bites and to seek medical attention for fever, severe headache, joint and muscle pain, or bleeding symptoms.
